JSON telemetry schema (SI units)
{ "timestamp":"ISO-8601", "temperature_c":25.4, "pressure_hpa":1008.2,
 "humidity_percent":58, "inclination_deg":12.5, "horizontal_velocity_mps":3.2,
 "vertical_velocity_mps":-1.4, "total_velocity_mps":3.49, "altitude_m":120,
 "latitude_deg":26.7606, "longitude_deg":83.3732, "range_m":250,
 "roll_deg":4.2, "pitch_deg":8.1, "yaw_deg":32, "acceleration_mps2":9.7,
 "battery_voltage_v":7.4, "battery_percent":85, "signal_dbm":-70,
 "freefall_detected":false, "impact_detected":false, "sensor_status":"ONLINE" }
All fields optional. Missing → shown N/A. Out-of-range or non-numeric → rejected and flagged. Altitude = above ground level (AGL), up = positive. Horizontal velocity = ground speed; course from successive GPS fixes (clockwise from north). Roll/pitch/yaw in aerospace ZYX convention. If absent, the dashboard calculates (tagged CALC): total velocity = √(h²+v²), vertical velocity from filtered altitude differences, inclination from roll/pitch, range from lat/lon/alt to the ground station at 26.7606, 83.3732 (edit GS in source). Free fall is derived from acceleration below the threshold for 3 consecutive samples above 5 m, and is not the same as descending.
Hardware (Arduino → PC → WebSocket)Arduino prints one JSON line per sample at 9600 baud, e.g. {"altitude_m":120.4,"pressure_hpa":1008.2,"temperature_c":25.4,"acceleration_mps2":9.8}. Send only what your sensors measure (BMP280: pressure, temperature, altitude; MPU6050: acceleration, roll, pitch; GPS: lat/lon). 
// bridge.js  —  npm i serialport ws
const {SerialPort,ReadlineParser}=require('serialport'),{WebSocketServer}=require('ws');
const port=new SerialPort({path:'COM3',baudRate:9600}); // /dev/ttyUSB0 on Linux
const p=port.pipe(new ReadlineParser({delimiter:'\n'}));
const wss=new WebSocketServer({port:8080});
p.on('data',l=>{try{const j=JSON.parse(l);j.timestamp=new Date().toISOString();
 wss.clients.forEach(c=>c.send(JSON.stringify(j)))}catch(e){}});
Run node bridge.js, open this page locally, choose “Real hardware”, Connect. ESP32/radio receivers can send the same JSON over WebSocket directly. Browsers on https pages block ws://localhost, so open the file locally.
Simulation vs hardwareSimulation generates synthetic pad → ascent → free fall → parachute descent → impact flights; everything is tagged SIM/CALC. Hardware mode shows only what arrives (MEAS), calculated values (CALC) or N/A. GPS, humidity, orientation and range need the matching sensors or ground-station data.
